Teaching map · K–5, 6th, 7th, 8th

Science Lessons, K–5 to 8th Grade

Open any file in a web browser (internet needed for fonts only). All 32 interactive lessons, sorted into K–5, sixth, seventh and eighth grade folders, are listed in a recommended teaching order, with what each builds on. Tap a unit to open it. Every lesson also links to related pages at the bottom and mentions earlier ideas at the top ("you may already have learned").

How to use this map

Start with the K–5 How Science Works unit (Unit 0: origins of science, the scientific method, hypotheses, fair tests). Then follow the numbered order, now split into the k-5/, 6th/, 7th/ and 8th/ folders. Units 10 to 13 are core sixth-grade units. Suggested sixth-grade order: 1, 2, 10 (States of Matter), 3, 11 (Earth in Space), 4, 5, 6, 13, then 7, 8, 9, 12. Do Unit 11 before Unit 4 (Weather) so the Sun’s heating and Earth’s tilt are already familiar. Units 8 (Classifying Life) and 14 (Where We’re Going) are optional extensions. Seventh and eighth grade continue in order. Sixth grade starts at Unit 1 once the K–5 method unit is done. Each unit is about five 30-minute sessions. Every lesson ends with a short browser game that practices its core idea; no install or login is needed.

Science Arcade

Six quick browser games (gravity, light, circuits, levers, states of matter, football physics) for warm-ups and rainy days: open the Science Arcade. Every lesson above also has its own game built in at the end.

K–5

Start with Unit 0 (how science works), then follow your grade: three units for each of Kindergarten, Grade 1 and Grade 2, then four, five and four for Grades 3, 4 and 5. Each unit covers one grade’s Michigan performance expectations. K2.0 is an optional warm-up for the youngest students.

Not covered yet

Units that are still missing from the plan: Earth's climate and climate change (beyond Unit 13), human body health topics (nutrition and a fuller treatment of disease; Unit 9 has a short immune-system section), chemistry of acids and bases, simple machines and work, and data analysis and statistics as its own mini-unit. High school is out of scope.

Standards mappings (NGSS performance expectations) in each lesson footer are approximate and should be checked against the OpenSciEd alignment pages and the Michigan Science Standards. Source programs: OpenSciEd and Michigan Virtual. This map is a plan, not an official Ann Arbor Public Schools sequence.
